newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks end 0.8 pct down on U.S. weakness.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks end 0.8 pct down on U.S. weakness.

text.p: SPI Sycom cl 2715.0 -31.0 US 30yr cl 6.45 -0.15
10yrbond futs 93.545 -0.140 Gold NY 324.65 Asia 324.50
AUD US$0.7390 (Friday US$0.7438) CRB Index cl 243.36 +0.61
*Stocks end broadly down after Friday's U.S. losses. Thin trade due to bank holiday in NSW. Volume 216.68 million, A$421.24 million value, 1,088 stocks traded, 339 steady, 255 up, 494 down.
The Australian share market ended 0.8 percent lower on Monday in reaction to U.S. weakness on Friday, but turnover was meagre as a bank holiday in New South Wales sidelined many investors.
"There was not much happening today, because we just didn't have the weight of money, with it being a bank holiday here," said one Sydney-based dealer.

The All Ordinaries index closed 21.5 points down at 2,706.0 in turnover of only A$421 million, about half the normal total. September share price index futures fell 31 points to 2,715, a mere nine point premium to the underlying market.
Banking shares suffered the most as sharply higher bond yields, triggered by a weak U.S. bond market, took its toll on the sector and pulled the index 1.1 percent lower.
Among the major banks, ANZ ended 19 cents lower at A$10.51 and National Australia Bank 14 cents down at A$19.37. Westpac Banking Corp lost 16 cents or almost 1.9 percent to close at A$8.46.

The big resources stocks ended mixed. BHP closed 16 cents lower at A$17.85, while Rio Tinto lost 12.3 cents to A$20.67. Gold and nickel producer WMC rebounded from early losses to end six cents firmer at A$7.70.
Dealers said there was no news behind WMC's gains, but that the stock had been come down to attractive levels recently.
There were few domestic factors driving the market on Monday, but this could change with the next few weeks' many upcoming half and full-year company results, dealer said.
"Maybe we'll get a bit more domestic direction from figures later this week, including labour force data on Thursday, and with the reporting season starting," one Brisbane-based dealer said.
Most listings with earnings reports due this week lost ground in line with the overall market.

Soft-drink group Coca-Cola Amatil recovered some early losses, but still ended 11.2 cents down at A$16.138 ahead of Wednesday's first-half profit announcement. The bottler is seen showing a slightly better net profit of about A$60 million for the half year to June 30, up from A$58.9 million a year ago.
"They are coming off a very weak base in the second half of last year," a Sydney-based analyst said.

Agricultural and chemicals group Wesfarmers lost 19 cents to A$12.09 ahead of Tuesday's full-year report, while diversified manufacturer Pacific BBA ended six cents weaker at A$5.64 ahead of its half-year report, also on Tuesday.

News Corp fell four cents to A$6.09. Dealers said some analysts had lowered their 1996/97 profit forecasts for the media group following poor box office performance of the Fox movie Speed 2: Cruise Control.

Foster's Brewing Group ended two cents softer at A$2.59, apparently unaffected by news that its Mildara Blass unit plans to buy Cellarmasters Pty Ltd for a total of A$160 million, a deal expected to be earnings positive from day one.
Taipan Resources, which recently reduced its dependency on gold exploration by buying the Marlborough nickel project in central Queensland, was Monday's most traded stock.
Taipan rose 0.5 cents to 11 cents in total volume of 13.22 million shares.
The number of declining stocks more than doubled advancing issues, and most of the day's winners had only small turnover.
Gold miner Plutonic Resources, one of last week's best performing stocks in the wake of a strong quarterly report, fell six cents to A$3.94.

Last week's most outstanding loser, Davids lost another five cents to A$0.84 as investors continued to pull out after Wednesday's news that the grocery retailer and wholesaler had made a A$262 million abnormal writedown.
Qantas Airways, which was hurt last week by rumours of a new Australian competitor being formed, recovered two cents to end at A$3.02.

Following the U.S. bond market, the Australian 10-year bond yield jumped 13 basis points to 6.47 percent in thin holiday trade, while the Australian dollar traded at US$0.7390/95 at 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), down from Friday's US$0.7433/38.
The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) is not expected to make any policy changes at its monthly meeting on Tuesday after last week's interest rate cut from to 5.0 percent from 5.5 percent.
